- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 3–5 periods.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast) — if true outcome deviates >2% from historical mean, adjust forecast toward historical mean.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-forecast horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast slope or add 1–2% upward bias in next 2–3 periods.  
- Model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods — increase forecast standard deviation by 10–20% if sentiment >0.7 for 3+ consecutive days.
